instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Orders from the Shadows
cards.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The crates went to Leeds. Send the driver to me, please. We correct the route before we circulate blame.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your email says Leeds. Shall I forward it to the manager?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forward the corrected address. That's the current instruction; don't send her an obsolete one to act on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants a timeline before approving another van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at 'Error discovered.' Then list my recovery steps. Exact times, please; leave the old order out of the recovery report.

beats.text: I'll rebuild the cancelled wedding bookings. Give the couples replacement dates, please, not a running commentary on the fault.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then don't use restore. Enter new bookings from the original dates; I'll read them out. Send new confirmations, please, not cancellation histories.

cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Not Up for Debate
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as cafe shift leader, please. Then give me tomorrow's milk order in litres, not 'about the usual.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who put you in charge? I usually do the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can give me an exact quantity. Start with what's left in the fridge, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it, but I'm writing 'appointment unconfirmed' beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use a clean stock sheet. Product, quantity, delivery date. No personnel notes, please; I need an order we can actually send.

beats.text: I'm inspecting the costume cupboard. Unlock it, please, and keep the velvet separate from the other fabric.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the director's name on the launch programme. We need one clear chain of command, not three department heads competing at the lectern.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my drawer. The programme is the running order, not a personnel bulletin. Please work from the approved names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: None. I'll read it on her behalf. Give all three the same length of introduction, please; don't promote anyone by adding a sentence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the treasurer's page out of the fair briefing. We can't have the stallholders replacing the chair before the gates open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Prepare it privately for after her welcome. Date and amount, please, but don't give her a debt form to sign at the microphone.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I send the workshop closure notice, name who backed your decision. 'Management' is not an adequate attribution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the approver. Who supported the proposal? Please don't collapse two different questions into one name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then list Sales as both supporter and beneficiary. Who authorised the space transfer? I need that name before this goes to the staff.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This roof proposal says 'we recommend.' Replace 'we' with names, please. I can't sign an anonymous recommendation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance backed the cheaper tiles. I need your signature to order them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the recommendation. Who authorised Finance to choose the tiles? Complete that line before we discuss my signature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The facilities director. The savings go into her office refurbishment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add both facts, please: her approval and where the savings go. Send that version to maintenance before asking me to sign.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've released the gallery from hosting my exhibition. They need time to develop their standards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected us. Shall I collect your paintings?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I'm withdrawing the work to give them that time. Carry the canvases upright, please, not in a stack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already put it outside. I'll bring the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'm yielding the frontage too. Cover the canvases before loading, please; do not let the gallery's standards become ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've handed you the chess-club chairmanship so you can develop. Start by checking tonight's fixture list, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for the match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'm releasing equipment control as well. Count the sets before handing them out; that's the proper sequence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Remove yourself as administrator too. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'm giving you independent control. Once I've removed my access, check every date before you publish. Independence still requires accuracy.
